problem.equation: partial_t u + (u dot grad)u + grad p = nu Delta u; div u = 0

claims.statement: For every Leray-Hopf solution with u0 in L2_sigma(R3), (1/2)||u(t)||_2^2 + nu int_0^t ||grad u||_2^2 <= (1/2)||u0||_2^2 for almost every t>0; the strong form holds for a.e. starting time s and all t>=s. Smooth decaying solutions satisfy equality for every 0<=s<=t.
claims.quantifiers: All nu>0, all such initial data, and all global Leray-Hopf solutions; smooth equality for every smooth solution interval.
claims.costs: Testing against u and integration by parts for smooth solutions; weak form is the defining energy inequality in the Leray-Hopf class.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the weak energy inequality in the stated Leray-Hopf definition, or a nonzero boundary/forcing term under the stated R3 unforced hypotheses.

claims.statement: Under u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), p_lambda=lambda^2 p(lambda x,lambda^2 t), ||u_lambda||_(Lq_t Lp_x)=lambda^(1-3/p-2/q)||u||_(Lq_t Lp_x); LqLp is critical exactly when 2/q+3/p=1. In particular, L-infinity_t L3_x and L5_t L5_x are critical, the L-infinity_t L2_x norm scales lambda^-1/2, and both its squared energy and integrated enstrophy budget scale lambda^-1.
claims.quantifiers: Every lambda>0 and every solution on R3 over a rescaled time interval; 1<=p,q<=infinity with the usual endpoint interpretation.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch in the transformed PDE or a change-of-variables computation contradicting the displayed exponents.

claims.statement: There is no uniform bound ||u||_(L5((0,T)xR3)) <= F(E0,D_T) over all smooth finite-energy unforced solutions and arbitrary finite T if F(a,b)->0 as a+b->0. In particular, no estimate with right-hand side C(E0+D_T)^alpha for fixed C<infinity and alpha>0 can hold uniformly.
claims.quantifiers: Fix nu>0 and any nonzero divergence-free Schwartz phi with Fourier support in an annulus; let v be any nonzero local smooth solution on [0,tau]. For every lambda>=1, the exact rescaled solution on T_lambda=tau/lambda^2 has E0=lambda^-1||phi||_2^2, D_T=lambda^-1 D_tau(v), and int|u_lambda|^5=int|v|^5=c_phi>0.
claims.costs: One standard local strong-existence fact plus exact parabolic scaling; no computation.
claims.missing_bound: A scale-invariant critical norm such as L5_t L5_x, or local pressure-aware critical smallness/flux control. The two global energy-budget values alone do not supply it.
claims.scope_limit: Rules out only scale-free closure from E0 and D_T alone that becomes small at the origin. It does not rule out estimates using T, critical scale ratios, profile data, pressure, or nonlinear flux, and implies neither blowup nor regularity.
claims.falsifier: A valid proof of such a uniform F estimate that survives the exact rescaled family, or an identified failure of a stated rescaling hypothesis.

claims.statement: For every nu>0 and finite T>0, a maximal H1 strong solution of the unforced 3D equations on R3 with divergence-free u0 in H1 and int_0^T ||u(t)||_5^5 dt<infinity satisfies sup_(t<T)||grad u(t)||_2^2<infinity and int_0^T||Delta u(t)||_2^2dt<infinity, and hence continues beyond T. Thus a finite maximal strong-solution time requires divergence of this critical integral.
claims.quantifiers: All nu>0, all finite T, and every maximal strong solution satisfying the stated data and finite Serrin integral.
proof_dependencies: Sobolev interpolation L2-L6 for grad u
claims.costs: The differential estimate is Y' + nu Z^2 <= C nu^-4 ||u||_5^5 Y; no numerical or external validation cost.
claims.falsifier: A smooth maximal H1 solution satisfying the finite L5 integral but failing the derived H1 bound or local continuation, or an error in the displayed differential estimate.

sources.reference: Jean Leray, Sur le mouvement d'un liquide visqueux emplissant l'espace, Acta Mathematica 63 (1934), 193-248.
sources.use: Original weak-solution construction and energy-dissipation inequality; primary PDF inspected.

sources.use: Historical primary source metadata only; not needed for the derivations in this note.

restart: Keep L5-CONTINUATION and ENERGY-ONLY-S5-NOGO fixed. State the next candidate as a fully quantified pressure-aware local critical-bound or flux estimate, then test it against parabolic concentration before any scale summation.
